campaign_conduct: The Tavily daily cap of 300 was respected on all three days. No provider limit was raised.
No new paid provider was enabled, DeepSeek search stayed off, no source restriction was bypassed, no source access was purchased, and no browser or captcha workaround was added.
No out-of-scope source project (SEDAR+ DDS, LSEG, browser automation, FCA FIRDS expansion, another search provider) was started.

Disclosure: early on day 1 the owner's personal email address was sent in the SEC User-Agent header for a few direct sec.gov fetches. This was corrected the same day. The same class of slip recurred on day 3 (2026-11-03): an evaluation subagent sent 4 SEC requests with the owner's personal email address as the User-Agent before it switched to the project's research contact string. The address is not reproduced here.
Deploy workflows have no concurrency guard. Rapid merges raced on day 1, and the db5baf8 smoke test failed and was superseded by the next deploy.
Budget and time stopped four planned reruns: CFR2, HON3, JPM2 and ADBE2 were not run. Their fixes are verified by offline replay only, or by the same mechanism on another company.

On 2026-11-03 only the Cellectis reruns CLLS4 and CLLS5 ran to prove #315-#317 live (56 Tavily credits). No other company was rerun after #315-#317; in particular LIN, whose iluka.com collision is the only one the #315 firewall replay found, was not rerun.

defects.title: A3 theme verification does not feed the industry hard constraint
defects.evidence: MEI/ILU/KNI: admission A3 verified_issuer (2-3 issuer passages, ILU/KNI 3 regulated) but constraint_results.industry = unknown, eligibility eligible_unverified, relevance_reason 'no verified statement of what the company does names the requested theme'
defects.expected: Theme-verified admitted names should pass (or at least not be 'unknown' on) the industry constraint and rank with registry names
defects.root_cause_hypothesis: pipeline.evaluate(): the industry constraint reads registry classification/screening only; the W6b A3 theme_evidence is not passed into it. relevance_reason is built from industry_result.basis

The report identifies Adobe correctly and handles the non-calendar fiscal year correctly for the hard numbers. FY2025 (FYE 2025-11-28) and Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-08-28) figures from XBRL reconcile exactly, and the FY2025 YoY of 10.53% uses the right fiscal comparison. Beyond that snapshot the research is stale, generic or wrong. It presents the FY2025 three-segment structure as current, although Adobe merged into one reportable segment in Q1 FY2026. It treats the Sept-10 Q3 results as an upcoming 'checkpoint' and never shows Q3 YoY growth (+12.9%), ARR ($27.50B) or the raised FY2026 targets on the investor page. It misses the CEO succession (Chakravarthy, effective 2026-12-01), the CFO resignation, the Semrush acquisition, the DOJ settlement and $6.8B of 9M buybacks. Competitive analysis names Tempus AI as a closest peer, the peer table prints cash conversion as 140.69×, and F14 shows FY2026 revenue as reported before the year has closed. The research state contradicts itself: it says the newest filing is the 10-K, marks the latest-period headline question 'not acquired' while holding those figures, and labels 10-K figures 'press; filing figure differs'. Most of the 61 open gaps are disclosed in documents the platform already acquired but extracted 0 facts from. The root causes are no software playbook, a max_tasks stop, skipped 8-K disclosures and failed issuer-document extraction.

This JPM report gets the identity right, and most individual figures it states (FY2025 revenue/NI/EPS, Q2 2026 NII, deposits, uninsured deposits, capital rollforward, ratings) reconcile exactly to the 10-K, the Q2 10-Q and XBRL. As bank research it fails. Its headline 'Total debt' (64,776m) is short-term borrowings only, with long-term debt of 435,206m silently dropped. Its executive synthesis and chair verdict lead with an industrial misreading of negative operating cash flow and a -259% 'cash conversion'. It blocks on missing EBITDA/FCF. The bank metrics that matter (provisions/NCOs, NPAs, CET1 for 2025, SLR, LCR, ROTCE, TBVPS, overhead ratio, NIM, segment results) are all in the 10-K/10-Q the platform acquired and indexed, yet the report asserts they were 'not acquired'. It misses the Q3 2026 results released 2026-10-13 because it ingested a 2026-10-20 note-offering 8-K as its 'results release'. The Q3 10-Q is not yet filed (live EDGAR, 2026-11-01, latest 10-Q 2026-08-06). Catalysts and risks are filled with FASB effective dates, J.P. Morgan SE governance, a stale interchange trial and a 2023 First Republic page. Meanwhile the Apple Card portfolio acquisition and the $4.6B Visa gain behind the Q2 profit are absent from the V3 research. A subsidiary's ICAAP leaks into the executive synthesis as group capital adequacy. Overall usefulness is about 3/10, on par with Honeywell before fixes.

The report gets PayPal's identity and every FY2025 XBRL figure and ratio right, and it correctly withholds total debt and keeps FCF and cash conversion. Beyond that it is thin and partly wrong. The latest Q3 2026 release (Item 2.02 EX-99.1) and the 10-Q were acquired and indexed, but the research state says the latest period's headline figures were 'not acquired'. Q3's direction (GAAP OI -8%, NI -14%), TPV, TM$, guidance and buybacks all go unreported, and stale Q2 product numbers from a chargeback blog stand in as the current picture. The legal picture is wrong. The 2022 class action is called 'resolved' though it is on appeal. The active 2026 Branded Checkout securities action is omitted. A gap claims no live regulatory action or litigation, despite FTC, CFPB, FCO and FCA proceedings in the 10-Q. Because the company is unclassified, no payments playbook ran: the synthesis frames customer balances as leverage, and the web follow-up searched for PayPal's 'nameplate capacity'. The CEO change, the buybacks that exceed FCF, and the €65bn BNPL forward-flow are missing. Usefulness is about where Honeywell stood before its fixes: right numbers, wrong or missing analysis.

This rerun keeps every FY2025 and Q3 XBRL figure correct and fixes two before-run errors: the red team's misdated cash and the 'resolved' class-action misreading, though the second is fixed only because litigation now does not appear at all. ADR-076 is mechanically live. The headline-figures question now searches the corpus and runs a recency pass, which brought in issuer-sourced Q3 active accounts (440M) and transactions (6,796M). The Q3 economics a payments analyst needs are still absent although the release is held: TPV $487.1B, TM$, the GAAP OI -8% / NI -14% decline, FCF, debt of $13.5B, the $1.5B buyback and the guidance table. The research state contradicts itself: one finding names the July release as the latest issuer disclosure, and a gap says no Q3 10-Q or press release is in evidence, beside findings that cite both. The worst new defect is a P0: the executive synthesis presents a Stripe/Advent $53B takeover offer 'rejected by the board' as fact, on a single unclassified web page that no filing supports. Litigation and regulation are falsely reported as absent, the chair dates Q2 third-party product growth to Q3, and the company remains unclassified, so no payments playbook ran. Net usefulness is unchanged at about 3: one important improvement is offset by a new fabricated-looking catalyst at the top of the report.

That happened because the claim was not regenerated, not because the ADR-078 gate fired: the editor rejected nothing for material_event_unvetted_source and the chair did not fall back. The report identifies Antofagasta correctly. The Antofagasta-specific numbers it does state, mostly FY2024 revenue bridge items, net debt and capex, match the issuer's FY2024 results, and its Q3 2026 output and cash-cost findings are correct. But the financial core is two periods stale: FY2025 results and H1 2026 financials were never acquired, and the synthesis presents Dec-2024 net debt of $1.6bn as a 'manageable' current position when net debt was $3.97bn at 30 June 2026. A third of the ledger is other companies (South32, Lundin, Ecora). The risk section and the executive synthesis attribute Lundin Mining's Vicuña JV and stakeholder risks to Antofagasta, and the 'stable labour' claim is contradicted by the October 2026 Centinela strike. A manufactured conflict shows Antofagasta 2024 'revenue' as $156.6m (a volume variance) against South32's $8,296m. ADR-071 did not catch it, because each side states one amount and neither names a segment. The issuer's own IR pages are labelled 'reported in the press' and counted as zero issuer documents, so ADR-065's label fix does not reach non-US issuers without a sourced website. With no classification, no mining playbook ran: reserves, royalty, attributable basis, price sensitivity and the 2027 commissioning catalysts are all missing. Overall usefulness is below the pre-fix Honeywell baseline.

The rerun fixes the two worst defects in the before report. No other company's facts are filed as Antofagasta's (0 of 40, against 10 of 35 before): the ADR-074 guard dropped a South32 statement and recorded an entity_ambiguous gap. The manufactured revenue conflict is gone: the '$156.6m' volume variance now sits beside the $6,613.4m revenue with no conflict. Risks and the synthesis are now Antofagasta's own (the Centinela strike and the royalty law), and the current catalysts are right (2027 commissioning, 2027 guidance 630-690kt). But the financial core is still FY2024. Group FY2025 and H1 2026 revenue, EBITDA and net debt were not extracted, and the synthesis still calls net debt 'manageable' from Dec-2024 data when it was $3.97bn at June 2026. A new scope error labels Centinela's segment capex ($1,414.0m for 2024, $2,478.1m for 2025) as Group capex. Q3 2026 production and the cost-guidance revisions dropped out when the fused Q2/Q3 statement was discarded. Issuer IR pages are still labelled press or 'Unclassified', with 0 findings counted from issuer documents. The company is still unclassified, so no mining playbook ran. Overall it is a real improvement (2 to 4), still well short of a usable report.

The report researches Cellectis as a Euronext-only issuer (ALCLS·PA). It never links the Nasdaq ADS line (CLLS, 1:1) or CIK 1627281, so no 20-F or 6-K was read and the SEC path was skipped as 'not an SEC registrant'. Its 30 findings rest on old cellectis.com documents and trade press. The newest period is Q1 2024, ten quarters behind the Q2 2026 results filed on 2026-08-06. The historical figures it quotes are accurate against filings, but they are stale and several are labelled 'reported in the press' although they are filed interim financials. The single most material event, the 2026-09-14 exit from lasme-cel/eti-cel and pivot to in vivo .HEAL programs with a restructuring and an H2 2028 runway target, was ingested as a web document but never became a finding. The chair therefore describes a CAR-T company that no longer exists and asserts that 'no FY2024 results [are] available'. Biotech essentials are absent: cash ($169m), burn (~$21m per quarter), runway, pipeline stage, AZ's ~32%/40% control and convertible preferred dilution. The legacy council saw only EODHD price data and reads momentum as fundamentals. The entity firewall mostly holds (no other company's facts are filed as Cellectis's), and there is no ADS double-counting, but only because the ADS line is absent altogether. Overall the report would mislead a reader about strategy, pipeline and financial position.

Two fixes worked, one did not, and the P0 is unchanged. The ADR-076 amendment works as designed. The recency window anchored on the newest held disclosure (the 2026-10-28 .HEAL 6-K, an issuer filing), ran 75 days from 2026-08-14, and pulled in both the H1 2026 6-K/A (F15/F16) and the 2026-09-14 pivot 6-K (F14/F17). 20-F chunks are now dated, and ADR-077's 6-K/A slot is finally read. The pivot reaches findings as an exit statement plus accession numbers tagged with the wrong periods (2027-H2, 2028-H2), and there is no .HEAL program, no runway, no cash and no burn. The report gets Lindian's JORC reserve and resource, granted Malawi licences, 100% SARECO ownership, Carester offtake terms, Gerald termination and interest-only FY26 income right, from real ASX documents. Its central financial picture is stale. It presents A$108m cash (30 Jun) and 'a cash position sufficient to start operations', although the acquired Sep-2026 Appendix 5B shows A$45.1m after a A$62.8m one-quarter draw, and no runway is computed. The executive synthesis wrongly says Lindian already 'mines and sells' concentrate, when first concentrate is only targeted for December 2026. The most material 2026 jurisdiction risk is absent: Malawi's raw-mineral export order, the draft beneficiation regulations, and the August suspension and parliamentary scrutiny. The rerun on 95ba5f7 is better than 796b644d on currency. It correctly names the 26-Oct Sep Quarterly and Appendix 5B as the newest disclosure, states 30-Sep cash of A$45,087k (from A$107,936k) and the quarter's A$24m project spend and A$28.8m SARECO payment, and gives the November energisation and December first-concentrate targets. The 'mines and sells' error is gone, but only because the editor failed (LLMJsonError) and the executive synthesis fell back to a first-finding-per-section list that says nothing about cash, timing or risk. The financial section is still wrong in substance: it presents koalagains' FY2025 figures (cash A$3.49m, equity A$58.4m, +0.98% shares) as the 'most recent fiscal year', computes no runway (5B 8.7 = 4.50 quarters, ~1.3 with capex), and a gap still says no post-placement cash exists. Entity separation is still broken: Lindian's own AR risk boilerplate is the counter-thesis, labelled 'Iluka's', and Iluka's zircon unit costs answer Lindian's unit-cost question without a name. Gaps still deny ownership, offtake volumes, cash and acquisition spend that findings state, and the V2 memo still says no issuer document exists. Malawi's export-order and beneficiation regime, the August suspension, Wei's retirement, the November meeting, dilution and the Stage 2 DFS are absent, and new tenement errors appeared. Usefulness 4/10 (was 3).

defects.title: Peers = Swatch only; sensitivities 'no research question assigned'
defects.root_cause: Peers limited to held companies

defects.title: Report presents a dissolved three-segment structure as current
defects.root_cause: Segment findings come only from the 10-K corpus. Nothing compares the segment perimeter across the 10-K and the newer 10-Q, and the editor writes in the present tense from undated findings (period_key None on F1).

defects.title: Filing-backed figures are badged 'Reported in the press; a filing figure differs' and tagged secondary_web
defects.root_cause: ev:c:1053a9a4… (source dated 2025-11-28, the FYE) is probably a 10-K copy or exhibit fetched by the web leg. Source-kind classification uses the fetch channel, not the document. The 'filing figure differs' check probably compares against XBRL canonical keys that have no segment dimension, so any segment figure counts as 'differs'.
defects.fix: #304 49ec531 ADR-071 fixes the contradiction badge. The 'secondary_web' source kind on a 10-K copy and 'not from a filing' on filed figures are not fixed. ADBE not rerun.

defects.title: F14 states FY2026 total revenue as reported from a non-existent 'Q4 2026 summary'
defects.root_cause: The web-finding extractor does not test whether a period has closed (FY2026 ends ~2026-11-27). Fiscal-period resolution for non-calendar FYs does not reject future periods, and the guidance-versus-actual distinction is not enforced on secondary_web findings.
defects.fix: #309 (ADR-072) shelved after 4 review rounds of false drops; needs a statement-kind tag at extraction (P-10).

defects.title: Peer set is Tempus AI and Alphabet
defects.root_cause: Peer selection is restricted to 'held companies' in the same coarse canonical industry ('Software & IT Services'). Tempus AI (SIC 7372-like) shares the bucket, and there is no similarity check on business description.

defects.title: Research state contradicts itself about the latest filing and the latest-period figures
defects.root_cause: Investigator prompts see a filtered evidence subset ('Two get_sec_statements items and eight search_company_corpus items were retrieved but excluded from this prompt'). gap_reconciliation does not match secfin:* evidence against corpus-derived question contracts, and the completeness agent's missing-source list is not fed by core_filings.

defects.title: Cash conversion printed as '140.69×' (and GOOGL '124.62×') in the peer table
defects.root_cause: The peer-table renderer applies a multiplier formatter to a field stored as a percentage (cash_conversion stored ×100).
defects.fix: #303 95772d0. Not exercised live: ADBE not rerun; PYPL had no peer table.

defects.title: Material post-period and in-period events are missing: CEO succession, CFO resignation, Semrush, DOJ settlement, buybacks
defects.root_cause: core_disclosures skipped ('venue_not_covered'), so 8-K Item 5.02 events are not ingested for Nasdaq. The catalyst investigator ran only 3 tool calls, the loop stopped on max_tasks, and the web leg spent its queries on 'nameplate capacity'.

defects.title: Q3 FY2026 results are treated as an upcoming event and the release content is not used
defects.root_cause: There is no event-date-versus-as-of check on catalyst findings. Release extraction produced 0 validated facts (the issuer-document extractor failed on the 8-K exhibit). The prior-year quarter is not in the canonical slots, so YoY is not derived, and the correct council YoY claims may be among the '8 council statements withheld' for not reconciling.
defects.fix: #305 d576570 ADR-068 makes the Item 2.02 EX-99.1 readable and #312 ADR-076 routes recency questions to it (live on PYPL2). ADBE not rerun, so the ADBE case is unverified.

defects.title: No issuer facts extracted from the acquired 10-K, 10-Q or 8-K
defects.root_cause: The issuer-document fact extractor or validator rejects Adobe's 52/53-week period headers ('Three Months Ended August 28, 2026') or the scope rules. The quarterly corpus row was reused with no chunks and reacquired (core_filings note).

defects.title: No software playbook; an industrial template drives the questions and web queries
defects.root_cause: Playbook coverage gap, with a generic fallback template that includes capacity and commodity questions.

defects.title: Stale balance-sheet framing in the chair and findings
defects.root_cause: Balance-sheet findings use only FY2025 secfin slots. The Q3 secfin slot set lacks debt (only cash, assets, equity and operating income were read).

defects.title: Derivative-suit finding has the wrong venue and count
defects.root_cause: The LLM summarised a truncated chunk boundary of Note 13 and generalised the venue.

defects.title: Filler and trivia ranked as catalysts and counter-thesis
defects.root_cause: There is no materiality filter on findings, and meta statements about evidence pass because 'statements_about_evidence' is 0, so the detector misses this phrasing.

defects.title: Ambiguous fiscal labels and contradictory period tiles
defects.root_cause: The period-label formatter drops the FY prefix, and the reporting_periods latest_interim slot is null while latest_quarter is set.

defects.title: Duplicate findings, stale-source citations and inconsistent gap counts
defects.root_cause: Dedup is by finding text, not by evidence set. The web leg ingests old sec.gov 10-Ks without a recency preference.

defects.title: 'Total debt' shown as 64,776m = short-term borrowings only; long-term debt (435,206m) omitted
defects.root_cause: The SEC XBRL snapshot mapper builds total_debt from whichever debt concepts exist for the period. JPM stopped tagging us-gaap:LongTermDebt after 2013 (it uses other LTD concepts or extension elements), so the stale-period guard dropped LTD and the sum silently degraded to ShortTermBorrowings, still labelled 'total_debt' and 'sourced_fact'. A partial sum is never flagged as partial. D/E and EV inherit the error.
defects.fix: #307 75c5389 ADR-067 (replay: 64,776 -> 499,982). JPM not rerun. Live on PYPL the withholding path holds, but no withheld reason reaches the page (PYPL-11).

defects.title: Latest quarter missed: wrong 8-K ingested as 'results_release'; Q3 2026 results absent
defects.root_cause: The results-release selector in the core-filings/current-period acquisition takes the latest 8-K (or the latest 8-K with Item 9.01 exhibits) without requiring Item 2.02 or an EX-99 earnings exhibit. Frequent issuers (banks file 8-Ks for every note offering) push the earnings 8-K out of the 'latest' slot. The ingestion then extracts 0 facts and nobody notices, because 'documents attempted 2 / extracted 2 / failed 0' reads as success.
defects.fix: #305 d576570 ADR-068 (replay resolves the 2026-10-13 Item 2.02 EX-99.1). JPM not rerun. Live on PYPL the EX-99.1 is read and, after ADR-076, feeds a finding.

defects.title: Industrial cash-flow and leverage semantics applied to a bank and promoted to the executive synthesis and chair verdict
defects.root_cause: The sector playbook (banks_financials) steers the V3 question graph, but the deterministic calculation layer (secfin:*:cash_conversion, net_margin), the snapshot completeness schema (required ebitda, self_critique) and the valuation-readiness gate are sector-agnostic. The editor and chair then treat a deterministic 'adverse' calc as the top financial signal.
defects.fix: #308 fbb40e8 ADR-069. JPM not rerun; the bank path was not exercised live. Live on PYPL a non-bank keeps FCF and cash conversion.

defects.title: Core bank metrics recorded as 'not acquired' although the acquired 10-K/10-Q and the platform's own XBRL contain them
defects.root_cause: (a) The statement-fact extractor targets an industrial line set (revenue, EBITDA, FCF and so on) and has no bank KPI schema, so facts_read=0 from bank filings. (b) Investigator retrieval over the corpus is query-shaped and only 1 corpus query ran in the whole run ('0 corpus queries' for 14 of 15 domains), so questions were answered from web pages and the gap writer asserted absence. (c) There is no reconciliation of gaps against XBRL facts the platform already holds.

defects.title: Executive synthesis attributes a subsidiary's (J.P. Morgan SE) ICAAP to the Group; subsidiary findings crowd group sections
defects.root_cause: The scope label is held only in the finding's prose (scope_key is None on these findings), so the editor's citation and figure checks cannot see an entity mismatch. The web-search leg admits jpmorgan.com subsidiary reports as issuer-domain sources.

defects.title: Council/red-team claims with wrong period and scope (H1 as Q2, Corporate segment as Firm) and wrong ROE
defects.root_cause: Legacy council claims are verified for citation presence and numeric reconcilability against canonical financials only. The numeric guard does not hold segment NIR or six-month columns, so a three/six-month column swap and segment/firm scope swaps pass. The ROE is the platform's own NI / ending total equity calculation.

defects.title: Stale facts used where the acquired filings hold newer ones; a resolved trial shown as pending
defects.root_cause: Web copies of the annual report (dated 2025-04-06 / 2026-04-05) outrank corpus chunks in retrieval. No supersession pass compares a finding's period with the newest acquired period for the same topic.

defects.title: Material Q2 2026 one-off (the $4.6B Visa gain) and filed corporate actions absent from V3 research
defects.root_cause: The catalyst domain ran 3 tool calls and 0 corpus queries, so it worked off generic web chunks. The 10-Q MD&A executive overview, where both items sit, was never queried.

defects.title: Irrelevant or junk findings fill sections (PJM capacity prices, FASB effective dates as catalysts, meta-findings)
defects.root_cause: The completion rule counts settled questions, so any finding settles a question. The investigator lacks a 'nothing material found' outcome and writes findings about the evidence itself. The web-date extractor took a page date that conflicts with the content.

defects.title: Source labels and page-header inconsistencies
defects.root_cause: The web-source classifier does not map the jpmorganchase.com IR domain to the issuer. The page header reads different state keys (latest_interim null vs latest_quarter).

defects.title: Blocking bank questions marked 'answered/satisfied' without the metric they ask for
defects.root_cause: The contract check counts trusted findings or evidence items and distinct sources (the acquisition_log 'trust' rung meets=true), not metric presence or period freshness. The playbook's required_metrics are not wired into the question contract. So 'all_blocking_questions_answered' is trivially met, and the run stopped with 'completion rules satisfied'.

defects.title: Latest results release acquired but unused; 'headline figures of latest period' reported as not acquired
defects.root_cause: Two layers. (1) The investigator/question layer: the results-release excerpts land in the primary-document artifact but are not fed into the V3 evidence pool or corpus search for the recent_external_developments question, which only tries web search (1 external search used). (2) facts_read=0: the statement-fact extractor produced no validated facts from either the 10-Q or the ER, so financial_statements_state shows 'figures not yet extracted'.
defects.fix: #312 95ba5f7 ADR-076 gave a partial live gain on PYPL2 (Q3 active accounts 440M and transactions 6,796M from the EX-99.1). REGRESSED on PYPL3 3992aa1d: that Q3 issuer operating data is lost, the chair calls FY2025 and Q2 2026 the snapshot, and TPV, TM$, the Q3 decline, FCF, debt and guidance are still missing (PYPL3-2).

defects.title: Securities litigation misread as 'resolved'; active 2026 Branded Checkout class action omitted
defects.root_cause: The investigator summarised the first litigation paragraph (filing history) and the LLM chair inferred 'resolved' from it. Evidence selection took a bounded excerpt of Note 13 without its later paragraphs, so later status changes were not seen. There is no legal-status extraction rule.
defects.fix: The 'resolved' misreading is gone only because no litigation finding exists on PYPL2 or PYPL3; the active 2026 Branded Checkout action is still omitted (PYPL3-3).

defects.title: Gap says no live regulatory action or litigation, contradicting the acquired 10-Q and the report's own F13
defects.root_cause: The gap generator writes 'absence' gaps from the investigator's evidence window, not from the indexed corpus (357 10-Q chunks; 0 corpus queries in 13 of 14 domains). gap_reconciliation does not check the gap against the report's own findings (F13).
defects.fix: PYPL2 and PYPL3 gaps still say there is no fine, regulatory action or litigation, against 10-Q Note 13 (PYPL3-3).

defects.title: Payments balance sheet read with industrial leverage semantics in executive synthesis and chair
defects.root_cause: No payments playbook (unclassified, SIC 7389), so the generic leverage question and the financial_analyst prompt treat total liabilities as leverage. ADR-069 only declares not-meaningful metrics for banks. There is no customer-funds-aware leverage view for payment institutions.
defects.fix: Downgraded to P2 on the rerun: the synthesis is neutral, the red team still reads customer balances as leverage. PYPL3: 'manageable net debt position' on long-term debt alone (PYPL3-5); the red team was withheld by the safety gate.

defects.title: Red team dates FY2025 cash to 2026-09-30
defects.root_cause: The red-team LLM merged the 10-Q 'as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025' comparative wording with the FY2025 XBRL value. numeric_verification flagged the chair variants but the red-team key point is displayed unchanged (admin surface).
defects.fix: The rerun red team dates FY2025 cash correctly. No targeted fix.

defects.title: Company unclassified: no payments playbook, mining/industrial template questions and web queries
defects.root_cause: The classification taxonomy has no mapping for SIC 7389, and the description-based inference refused ('no unambiguous description'). The generic template carries industrial questions.
defects.fix: Still unclassified on PYPL2 and PYPL3; mining/industrial template questions persist ('PayPal nameplate capacity ramp-up').

defects.title: Stale, third-party Q2 product metrics presented as current
defects.root_cause: Web evidence outranks primary-document excerpts in evidence selection because the primary-document channel produced 0 facts. No recency check against the latest acquired period.
defects.fix: Escalated on PYPL2 (the chair splices the stale Q2 figures into a Q3 statement, PYPL2-5). On PYPL3 the chair dates them to Q2, but they are still third-party and Q3 is omitted.

defects.title: Capital allocation omits buybacks that exceed FCF
defects.root_cause: The secfin statement-line set used for findings lacks PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock, even though companyfacts has it.
defects.fix: Still present on PYPL3 (PYPL3-6).

defects.title: CEO change missing; gap says no executive disclosure
defects.root_cause: Catalyst window (90 days) and filing-body cap mean that only the 10-Q and Item 2.02 8-K are read. Item 5.02 8-Ks older than 90 days are not considered for governance.
defects.fix: Still present on PYPL3 (PYPL3-9).

defects.title: Research state contradicts itself on 10-Q coverage and question status
defects.root_cause: HTML excerpts carry page_number=null, rendered as page 1. Investigator tasks did not call search_company_corpus. Question contract satisfaction counts any finding, not one that answers the question.
defects.fix: The 'only page 1 of the 10-Q' gap is gone and 3 domains now query the corpus. Questions are still 'satisfied' with 0 findings; on PYPL3 competitive position is 'Evidenced' with no competitor (PYPL3-10).

defects.title: Total debt withheld without the ADR-067 reason; Q3 total that exists is called missing
defects.root_cause: debt_basis.withheld_reason is not carried into financial_snapshot/missing_information, and the old missing-field wording is reused. The annual-only bundle never derives a current-period total.
defects.fix: Still present on PYPL3 ('Required field missing'; the Q3 total called absent).

defects.title: Unconfirmed M&A rumours and an irrelevant article listed as current developments
defects.root_cause: The web catalyst list has no relevance filter or rumour flag. The source class is shown but claim status is not.
defects.fix: Worsened into the P0 PYPL2-1 on PYPL2. On PYPL3 the Stripe headline is still listed in Current developments, labelled, outside ADR-078's scope (PYPL3-11).

defects.title: numeric_verification withholds a correct chair statement as conflicting
defects.root_cause: numeric_verification attaches the first amount in a multi-figure sentence to a metric named by keyword. This is the ADR-071 single-claim rule, not applied in numeric_verification.
defects.fix: PYPL3: 4 conflicts, all false; 4 correct statements withheld (PYPL3-12).

defects.title: ISIN shown as a blocking identity gap
defects.root_cause: The legacy completeness agent treats ISIN as required.

defects.title: Unsupported takeover claim presented as fact in the executive synthesis
defects.root_cause: (1) The trust ladder has no claim type for corporate-control events, so a single-source unknown_web statement 'meets' the bar. (2) The executive-synthesis verifier checks citations, figures and prohibited words, not the source class or corroboration of the cited finding. (3) There is no rule that M&A/control claims need an issuer filing (8-K 1.01/7.01/8.01, SC 14D9, 425) or carry a 'reported' label like F13's.
defects.fix: #314 48b5777 ADR-078: a material corporate event resting only on unvetted web pages is never stated in the synthesis or chair output. Replay over all 13 stored reports blocks only this sentence, 0 false drops. Live on PYPL3 3992aa1d (48b5777) the takeover is absent, but the gate did NOT fire: the event analyst simply did not regenerate the claim (rejected_by_reason has no material_event_unvetted_source; the chair did not fall back). Not reproduced live; the fix is proven by replay only.

defects.title: Research state contradicts itself on what the latest issuer disclosure is
defects.root_cause: There is no post-check that a 'latest disclosure' finding's date is at least the newest held issuer document (2026-10-27). gap_reconciliation cannot match free-text gaps without a field ('field_unknown') against findings. ADR-076's acquired_not_read applies only to unresolved questions, and the gap knowledge_state taxonomy was left unchanged, so the gap still says 'not acquired'.
defects.fix: F10 calls the 2026-07-28 release the latest while other findings cite Q3; a gap denies the Q3 10-Q. Escalated in scope on PYPL3 (PYPL3-1): the chair key point says no issuer release or filing is in evidence.

defects.title: Chair splices Q2 third-party product growth into the Q3 results statement
defects.root_cause: The chair prompt receives findings with period_key=None for web findings (F2/F35 have no period_key although the text says Q2), so period-consistency checks cannot fire. numeric_verification does not cover percentages.
defects.fix: PYPL3: the chair dates the third-party product growth to Q2 instead of splicing it into Q3. No targeted fix: web findings still carry period_key None, so this is LLM behaviour, not a mechanism.

defects.title: Period and labelling slips
defects.root_cause: The investigator period_key is taken from the document, not the column. financial_statements_state counts only the issuer-document fact channel and ignores the XBRL current-period channel.
defects.fix: PYPL3: the Dec-2025 comparatives finding is gone, but 'Latest interim: Not in this report' beside 'Latest quarter Q3 2026' and the ISIN blocking gap remain (PYPL3-14).

defects.title: Manufactured revenue conflict shows Antofagasta 2024 revenue as $156.6m against South32's $8,296m
defects.root_cause: trust.find_contradictions: _same_frame matches on period '2024' and scope None==None. field_clause isolates one amount on each side, so ADR-071's _money_disagree single-amount test passes, and neither clause names a segment, so _same_part passes. Nothing checks (a) that both sides are about the subject issuer (F1 names South32), or (b) that a 'reducing revenue by X' / variance clause is a change, not a revenue level, in the revenue field matcher.
defects.fix: #310 e052ec2 ADR-074 (a change is not a level; another company's statement on its own site is not the issuer's). ANTO2: no conflict; '$156.6m' sits beside revenue $6,613.4m.

defects.title: Cross-entity contamination: South32, Lundin and Ecora findings fill the business, competitive, financial and risk sections
defects.root_cause: The deep web crawl's competitive/risk query families ingested peer annual reports (south32.net, lundinmining.com). The investigator's another-company guard did not fire: with no issuer website/aliases sourced (profile.website missing, unclassified) it apparently has no subject-entity anchor, and statements that NAME another company were kept. The section assembler and editor do not filter on subject entity.
defects.fix: #310 e052ec2 ADR-074. ANTO2: other-company findings 10/35 -> 0/40; entity separation score 1 -> 7.

defects.title: FY2024 balance sheet and labour state presented as current in the synthesis and chair
defects.root_cause: The latest annual and interim reports were never acquired (NSM source_unavailable, no issuer-IR fallback for the results PDFs). The editor and chair have no as-of/freshness rule that stops a 2024-dated finding being written in the present tense.
defects.fix: Labour half fixed on the rerun (Centinela strike named). Net debt half open: the synthesis still calls Dec-2024 net debt 'manageable' ($1.6bn vs $3.97bn at 30 Jun 2026).

defects.title: F7 joins the Q3 guidance raise to the Q2 rationale and keys it 2026-Q2
defects.root_cause: The investigator merged two evidences into one statement, and the period key was taken from the older Q2 evidence. Guidance is a SUPERSEDABLE field, but no supersession chain is built, so the two revisions are fused rather than ordered.
defects.fix: The fused Q2/Q3 statement is now discarded by the period-agreement guard. Side effect: Q3 output and guidance vanished (ANTO2-2).

defects.title: Research state contradicts itself on what is the latest disclosure, and the chair invents a net-debt disagreement
defects.root_cause: The financial_statements_state reporting periods are derived only from issuer-document facts (0 read), so web-held 2026 releases never update the 'latest period'. The F18 investigator statement is not reconciled against later findings. The chair LLM (gpt-4.1-mini) narrates disagreements without a check against the conflict ledger.
defects.fix: Rerun: 'most recent disclosure covers full-year 2025' while H1 and Q3 2026 are cited.

defects.title: The issuer's own IR documents are labelled 'reported in the press' / 'Unclassified web page'
defects.root_cause: is_issuer_origin cannot verify the issuer domain: profile.website is not sourced for this LSE issuer, and aminerals.cl (the subsidiary) is not linked to the issuer. ADR-065's label fix depends on a 'verified issuer', which is missing for non-US names.
defects.fix: ADR-065's label fix does not reach an issuer with no sourced website.

defects.title: Latest annual and interim financials and the material 2026 events are absent
defects.root_cause: core_disclosures uk_fca_nsm: 'the London Stock Exchange's own record could not be read'. The company_docs query family found the 2024 AR but not the 2025/2026 results PDFs, and fetching stopped on budget:max_wall_seconds after 9 docs (57MB, 1,041 pages, mostly old ARs and peer reports).
defects.fix: Partly improved on the rerun (H1 2026 net cost, realised price, 2027 guidance) with no targeted fix; group FY2025/H1 2026 revenue, EBITDA and net debt still absent.

defects.title: The company is unclassified, so no mining playbook ran and the sector variables are missing
defects.root_cause: The classifier relies on SEC SIC or a stored sector. Non-US LSE names have neither, and no fallback reads the issuer's description or the corpus commodity terms.

defects.title: Attributable vs 100% basis is never stated; the mine split mixes bases and omits Centinela
defects.root_cause: scope_key has no 'attributable' vs '100%' dimension. The breakdown sentence inherits 'group', and the investigator dropped the basis qualifier from the table row label.
defects.fix: Not exercised on the rerun (no multi-mine split).

defects.title: Period keys missing on current findings
defects.root_cause: The ADR-065 key derivation runs on the evidence's period-end phrase. Web evidence from minelistings and the IR HTML pages without an 'ended' clause yields None, and the statement text ('Q3 2026', 'H1 2026') is not used as a fallback.

defects.title: The executive synthesis is two duplicated sentence pairs with no figures; the subject is called a 'Peer'
defects.root_cause: The editor's figure ban drops every quantitative sentence, and nothing removes duplicate sentences. The competitive investigator framed the subject from a peer-document perspective.
defects.fix: 'Peer Antofagasta' gone; duplicated synthesis sentences remain.

defects.title: Centinela segment capex presented as Antofagasta (Group) capex
defects.root_cause: The investigator extracted from the FY25 RNS 'CENTINELA — Capital expenditure was $2,478.1 million ...' paragraph. The mine heading sits outside the excerpt or chunk, so the sentence reads as group-level and is written with the issuer as subject. scope_key stays None. No check flags a figure taken from a segment section as Group, and the evidence text is web, so it bypasses the issuer-document segment-scope parser.
defects.fix: Centinela capex ($1,414.0m 2024; $2,478.1m 2025) labelled Group capex (Group: $2,414.9m; $3,684.5m).

defects.title: Regression: Q3 2026 production and cost guidance dropped out entirely
defects.root_cause: The period-agreement guard correctly discards a statement that fuses two periods. Nothing re-asks the question per period, and the follow-up rounds targeted capex, capacity and customers, not the latest quarter. The Q3 issuer page was not re-fetched (antofagasta.co.uk news pages are not in the ingest list this run).
defects.fix: Regression from the period-agreement discard: Q3 2026 output (151.9kt) and the 2026 guidance cut are gone.

defects.title: Gaps contradict findings in the same ledger
defects.root_cause: Each investigator task writes gaps from its own evidence slice, and gap_reconciliation only marks 'partially addressed' by field match (and mis-links some, e.g. a South32 gap to F1 and F26). There is no cross-task de-contradiction pass.

defects.title: Chair model unavailable; the deterministic chair is used
defects.root_cause: The Azure OpenAI chair call failed or was not configured at run time (5 azure calls were made, the red team among them). The fallback is honest, but the run is degraded.
defects.fix: Degraded state is recorded ('no chair model was available').

defects.title: Gap-to-finding links and knowledge-state labels are wrong for entity and period-discard gaps
defects.root_cause: gap_reconciliation matches on field (metric:revenue / net_debt) regardless of gap_type.

defects.title: Dual-listed SEC filer researched as a Euronext-only issuer: the CLLS/CIK sibling was never linked, so no 20-F/6-K was read
defects.root_cause: ADR-061 lives in Discovery's IdentityOutcome only. The Company row created from the candidate persists only ticker/exchange, without securities or an ISIN. filing_evidence.ensure_core_filings, classification and the SEC providers key on company.ticker/company.exchange via is_sec_eligible(exchange), and there is no sec_issuer_registry entry mapping ALCLS→CIK 1627281. 'Analyze a company' on a home line therefore never reaches the US line.
defects.fix: #311 09836d0 ADR-075 + #313 342b660 ADR-077: CIK 1627281 linked by SEC directory name and France domicile; 20-F FY2025 (1010 chunks, was 0) and, from CLLS3 on, the H1 2026 6-K/A (161 chunks) held and cited on CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5. The residue is not fixed and is tracked separately: facts_read=0 on every run (the XBRL reader is us-gaap only, IFRS is not read; CLLS3-2, CLLS5-1).

defects.title: The most material event, the 2026-09-14 strategic transformation (exit of lasme-cel/eti-cel, pivot to in vivo .HEAL programs, restructuring), was acquired but not used
defects.root_cause: recent_external_developments ran 0 external searches ('no citable evidence was retrieved'). The investigator questions consumed corpus/web items by intent and none routed the catalyst-family web document into a finding. globenewswire.com, the issuer's PR wire, returned HTTP 403, and the platform cannot use the SEC 6-K copy (see CLLS-1).
defects.fix: Missed on CLLS2 and CLLS3. After #316 (ADR-076 amendment) CLLS4 and CLLS5 state the exit from lasme-cel/eti-cel. .HEAL-101/201, their data dates and the H2 2028 runway are still absent (0 occurrences of '.HEAL'); the 6-Ks reach findings with forward dates as period tags (CLLS4-2, CLLS5-1).

defects.title: The chair states false facts about disclosure availability and presents a 2024 snapshot as the current state
defects.root_cause: The chair prompt synthesises from findings without a guard that turns 'not in evidence' into a platform gap. The legacy 8-agent council ran on a 5-item price-only evidence pack and reads momentum as fundamentals. There is no latest-period check against the regulator's filing list, because the SEC path was skipped.
defects.fix: Gone on the rerun after #311 09836d0: the council refused (blocking question open) and the chair fell back to a deterministic verdict. No guard was added that stops 'not in evidence' being stated as 'does not exist' (same class as PYPL2-1, LIN-1).

defects.title: The research state contradicts itself on what the evidence holds
defects.root_cause: The legacy council evidence pack is built from the financial-data agent (price/profile) independently of the V3 corpus/web findings. The recent_disclosure contract checks source presence, not document date versus the latest filed period.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5: the legacy council says 'No primary filings, financial statements, or company disclosures are present in the evidence pack' ('ALCLS on exchange PA is not SEC-eligible') while 14-16 findings cite issuer filings.

defects.title: The issuer's own site is classed unknown_web, and filed interim financial content is labelled '[reported in the press; not from a filing]'
defects.root_cause: The issuer domain is resolved from profile.website, which is 'not sourced' for this company, or via the SEC official-domain lookup, which is skipped for ALCLS·PA. With no issuer domain known, the trust ladder classes the IR site as unknown_web and the claim-type rule applies the press label to financial_statement claims.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS5: cellectis.com is an 'Unclassified web page'; 6-K exhibits labelled 'secondary web'.

defects.title: A biotech went unclassified: no playbook and non-biotech templates
defects.root_cause: Classification uses only the SEC SIC for SEC-eligible exchanges and the stored sector. The ALCLS row has neither, and Euronext has no classification connector. The generic web template mixes mining and industrial families.
defects.fix: #311 09836d0 ADR-075: SEC SIC 2836 -> Biotechnology; biotech playbook v1 applies. Mining templates still run beside it (CLLS2-7).

defects.title: Stale facts are presented without recency ranking
defects.root_cause: period_key is not populated for web/IR documents (29/30 findings have None), so supersession and recency checks cannot run. Corpus/web relevance does not penalise document age.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS3-CLLS5 (2019-2024 items and exited programs).

defects.title: Garbage scope keys parsed from sentence fragments and question text
defects.root_cause: The scope parser accepts any 'segment' phrase from the excerpt or the question prompt as a segment label, with no shape check (see the 'UNKNOWN scope fills a Group slot' trap).
defects.fix: Reduced from 2 instances to 1 on CLLS2; absent on CLLS3 and CLLS4 with no targeted fix; REGRESSED on CLLS5 (a cash-flow row label as a segment scope key, CLLS5-5).

defects.title: The whole professional report was withheld because the safety scan flagged one gap description
defects.root_cause: The final safety scan is all-or-nothing at the professional_research level. The substring-based gate probably matched a word in an auto-generated gap description.
defects.fix: Not exercised on the rerun (no passage flagged).

defects.title: Biotech economics are absent: runway, burn, AZ control/dilution and pipeline stages
defects.root_cause: This follows from CLLS-1 (no 20-F/6-K) and CLLS-6 (no biotech playbook contract to demand these variables).
defects.fix: No targeted fix. CLLS5 states Dec 2025 cash ($211M, from a web copy); there is still no current cash, burn, runway, current pipeline asset or AZ control figure.

defects.title: The AstraZeneca '$245m invested' figure conflates a collaboration upfront with equity
defects.root_cause: A trade-press headline figure was accepted at the guidance rung (single source). The issuer 20-F breakdown was not acquired.
defects.fix: Absent on CLLS2-CLLS4 with no targeted fix (F28/F31 used the 20-F's $80.0m IIA). REGRESSED on CLLS5: 'AstraZeneca invested $245m' is the Business-model lead and synthesis sentence 1 (CLLS5-3).

defects.title: The investor summary lists a negative signal as a value driver and repeats price-only boilerplate across 7 agents
defects.root_cause: The chair bullet slotting does not check polarity. The legacy council emits per-agent evidence restatements.
defects.fix: Absent on CLLS3 and CLLS4 too.

defects.title: The interim and current period of a 6-K filer is never acquired because the quarterly slot accepts only 10-Q
defects.root_cause: ADR-075 maps the annual form to 20-F for a foreign private issuer but leaves the quarterly form list at the domestic ['10-Q'] default. ensure_core_filings has no 6-K exhibit classifier (interim report vs press release).
defects.fix: #313 342b660 ADR-077: a 20-F filer's interim results are read from its results 6-K. Acquisition PROVEN LIVE on CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5: the quarterly slot holds the H1 2026 iXBRL 6-K/A 0001193125-26-389336 (period 2026-06-30, 161 chunks), selected among 21 listed 6-Ks. Use is not fixed: no figure on CLLS3, one net-loss line on CLLS4, none again on CLLS5 (CLLS3-2, CLLS5-1); facts_read=0 (IFRS not read).

defects.title: A former subsidiary's (Calyxt, now Cibus) risk factors are filed as Cellectis's counter-thesis
defects.root_cause: ADR-066's related-registrant check keys on the document's registrant or the statement's named subject. The text sits in the issuer's own 20-F, so the registrant matches, and the investigator paraphrased 'Calyxt' away. No subject check runs on parent-filing passages describing a subsidiary. The source is also 2022 and has no recency penalty.
defects.fix: No targeted fix (ADR-079 judges EDGAR web copies by CIK; this text sits in the issuer's own FY2022 20-F). Absent from the counter-thesis on CLLS3 and CLLS4; on CLLS5 F30 'limited operating history' (Calyxt's phrase in the FY2022 20-F) and F10 (Calyxt seed production) are back in Cellectis's sections.

defects.title: The chair and the tech block report 0 findings while the ledger holds 37, and the degraded reason is wrong
defects.root_cause: The deterministic fallback reads council.finding_count, which is 0 when the council did not convene, instead of the ledger count. The fallback-reason text is hard-wired to 'no findings'.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5: the chair says 'Deterministic synthesis: 0 finding(s) ... No model was available' and the tech block 'Findings 0' while the ledger holds 37 (CLLS3), 38 (CLLS4) and 32 (CLLS5); council.refusal_reason is blocking_question_open and the chair slot is routed to azure_openai.

defects.title: The blocking cash_runway question was never researched although the answer is in the acquired 20-F, and its gap is labelled 'not acquired'
defects.root_cause: These questions are wired to structured-fact tools (financial facts and XBRL) that return nothing for a 20-F, because the fact extractor handles 10-K/us-gaap only. No corpus_by_intent fallback runs for them. The knowledge_state classifier does not check whether core_filings holds the document.
defects.fix: No targeted fix. Round 0 of cash_runway still runs tools=[] on CLLS3-CLLS5. On CLLS5 web follow-up answers it with Dec 2025 cash $211M from a web copy, not the held June 2026 figure in the 6-K/A; the runway is absent and the gap is still rendered 'Not acquired by the platform'.

defects.title: The 20-F in the corpus is undated, so its findings carry no date or period and recency logic cannot run
defects.root_cause: The core_filings ingest records filing_date on the slot but not on the DocumentVersion published_at used by findings.
defects.fix: #316 a8f8f8a (ADR-076 amendment): SEC corpus chunks carry the EDGAR filing date, backfilled on re-encounter. Live on CLLS4: 20-F findings dated 2026-03-20, the 6-K/A 2026-09-11, the 6-Ks 2026-09-14 and 2026-10-28. Residual: findings mixing the 20-F with cellectis.com show no date.

defects.title: Unrelated companies appear as Cellectis 'Current developments', and the peers are irrelevant
defects.root_cause: catalyst_evidence admits any catalyst-family search hit with no subject check, and French-language queries pull Euronext Paris quote and news pages. The peer set falls back to the canonical-industry tag.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS3-CLLS5 (Vertex, a Sanofi quote page, Dassault Aviation, a vocational-school page; peers Moderna only).

defects.title: Mining and industrial templates still run on a classified biotech
defects.root_cause: The web_followup glossary and gap templates (w7.1) are not keyed by playbook. The biotech playbook only adds questions.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS3-CLLS5 ('Cellectis capacity expansion cost', 'nameplate capacity ramp-up'; template w7.1).

defects.title: Gaps contradict findings in the same report
defects.root_cause: Each investigator call writes gaps from its own 8-item evidence slice, and gap_reconciliation only checks council concerns, not cross-question gaps.
defects.fix: Still present on CLLS3-CLLS5 (CLLS5: 'no Cellectis cash balance is given' vs F21; no ownership evidence vs F23/F31).

defects.title: The identity record still shows one line, with no ADS, ISIN or reporting currency
defects.root_cause: ADR-075 resolves the SEC registrant at research time but does not persist the linked security or ADS ratio to the company identity record.
defects.fix: ADR-061's security list never reaches the company record. Unchanged on CLLS5 ('ALCLS · PA · Healthcare'; ISIN and LEI blocking).

defects.title: The editor failed and the investigator truncated 12 times
defects.root_cause: DeepSeek JSON output budget.
defects.fix: No targeted fix. The editor ran on CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5; investigator truncations were all recovered by retries (CLLS5: 18 of 18).

defects.title: Executive synthesis says the pre-revenue developer 'mines and sells monazite concentrate'
defects.root_cause: Editor model: F5 is phrased in the present tense ('mines and concentrates ... sells concentrate, not metal'), from a value-chain description, and the editor check verifies citations, figures and prohibited words but 'not meaning'. The stage classifier left stage=None (no_or_immaterial_revenue=false even though revenue is interest only), so nothing told the editor the company is pre-production.
defects.fix: Absent on the rerun only because the editor failed (LLMJsonError) and a deterministic synthesis was used. The tense/stage check does not exist.

defects.title: Cash/funding is stated at the 30-Jun figure; the acquired Sep-2026 Appendix 5B (cash A$45.1m, −58% in one quarter) is never used and no runway is computed
defects.root_cause: The statement-fact extractor reads no Appendix 5B layout (facts_read=0: $A'000 two-column 'current quarter / year to date' with item numbers 1.9/2.6/4.6/8.7). The cash_generation_and_funding question ranks the AR narrative above the 26-chunk 5B, and there is no 'later period supersedes' rule for cash. The mining playbook has no runway metric tied to the 5B.
defects.fix: #312 95ba5f7 ADR-076: the 30-Sep cash A$45.1m now appears (F32, under Catalysts). No runway is computed (5B item 8.7 = 4.50 quarters, about 1.3 with capex).

defects.title: Subject's own Annual Report statements filed as Iluka's
defects.root_cause: Investigator: the model saw Iluka named nearby in the AR chunk (the offtake/loan note) and named the speaker wrongly. The ADR-074-style subject firewall checks 'about another company' only for web origins; there is no check that issuer_filing text is the subject's own voice. Investigator diagnostics show statements_about_another_company=0.
defects.fix: #315 (2ea310a) made the ADR-066 publisher firewall live; its replay drops 4 (LIN) + 3 (LIN2) findings resting only on iluka.com, the only collision among 121 registered companies. LIN was not rerun after #315, so this is not proven live, and whether the drop removes every misattributed Annual Report statement is not established.

defects.title: Iluka (offtaker/lender) material crowds Lindian's questions, and Iluka is conflated with Lynas
defects.root_cause: Web follow-up and question routing: 'peer'-labelled statements still satisfy subject question contracts (topic slot filled = contract satisfied). The editor model paraphrases the lead across two findings without entity checks. iluka.com is classified 'unknown_web'.
defects.fix: #310 e052ec2 ADR-074 removed the Iluka net debt, outlook, disclaimer and environmental items and the Lynas conflation. Implicit-subject Iluka unit costs remain.

defects.title: Research state contradicts itself on which documents exist
defects.root_cause: The 'reused, not fetched' corpus documents (Sep Quarterly, 5B, Ops) are not passed to the recent_disclosure investigator's document list or to gap reconciliation. The V2 generator and memo read the legacy primary_documents pipeline (empty for ASX) rather than core_disclosures. Gap text is generated per investigator round and never re-reconciled against later findings (platform_evidence_gaps_reconciled=0).
defects.fix: 'No quarterly report is present' is gone; gaps still deny ownership, offtake, cash and acquisition spend that findings state; the V2 memo still says no issuer document exists.

defects.title: Chair invents a revenue contradiction and cites a disagreement id that does not exist in the council
defects.root_cause: Chair LLM (azure gpt-4.1-mini) reasoning over F3 and F54. The chair output validator does not check that unresolved_disagreement_ids exist in the ledger, or that a narrated conflict is backed by a recorded one.
defects.fix: The rerun chair's single disagreement matches a recorded red-team challenge. No validator was added.

defects.title: Material Malawi jurisdiction events missing
defects.root_cause: The ASX acquisition budget took only 5 of 224 listed documents (3 'results' + 2 other). Non-results price-sensitive announcements are not ranked by risk relevance, and the web permit queries returned generic pages.

defects.title: Dilution, capital structure and valuation inputs absent
defects.root_cause: No shares-outstanding extraction from ASX ARs (no XBRL; facts_read=0). The mining playbook does not require dilution or shares on issue.

defects.title: FY2026 financial statements acquired but not extracted (facts_read=0)
defects.root_cause: The statement-fact extractor fails on the two-column interleaved PDF text of Australian ARs (the pdf text interleaves pages 2-up). Same class as PYPL facts_read=0.

defects.title: Guinea tenement IDs assigned to the wrong projects; Lelouma's inactive status missed
defects.root_cause: Investigator reading a flattened table with a row label ('Lelouma Project3') split from its row values; no table-structure-aware extraction.
defects.fix: Worse on the rerun: 2020/2562 assigned twice, Woula dropped, granted Tanzanian licences called applications.

defects.title: Stale governance and risk items presented undated as current; current ones missed
defects.root_cause: There is no recency gate on governance or risk questions. source_published_at is shown in the evidence block but not in the statement. The web results' 2024 dates did not demote them.

defects.title: Aluminium market research for a rare-earths developer
defects.root_cause: subject_profile counts commodity mentions across 600 chunks (bauxite resource tables inflate them) without weighting by asset materiality or status. The canada.ca published_at is page metadata, not the content date.

defects.title: Trust labels and dates
defects.root_cause: ADR-065 origin match needs a verified issuer website, and none is held for LIN (profile.website missing). Date normalisation is UTC.

defects.title: Financial capacity shows FY2025 aggregator figures as 'most recent fiscal year'; the 30-Sep cash sits only in Catalysts; no runway
defects.root_cause: ADR-076's recency pass applies only to RECENCY_QUESTION_KEYS. cash_generation_and_funding and balance_sheet_risk (financial_analyst) still rank the corpus by ts_rank_cd without a window and fell back to web follow-up (koalagains). No rule checks a third-party 'most recent fiscal year' against the newest held annual period (FY2026 AR). With facts_read=0 there is no canonical cash slot for a newer figure to supersede, and gap reconciliation does not match F32 (period_key null, catalysts domain) to the cash gap.
defects.fix: Financial capacity shows koalagains' FY2025 figures (cash A$3.49m) as 'most recent fiscal year'.

defects.title: Editor failed; the executive synthesis is a first-finding-per-section list
defects.root_cause: Editor LLM returned unparseable JSON (deepseek/azure routed). The fallback picks each section's first finding by order, not by importance.

defects.title: Research state denies holding the issuer's Q3 release and 10-Q, and the chair repeats it as a key point
defects.root_cause: Investigator 'about the evidence' statements (statements_about_evidence=1) are judged only against the question's own retrieved items, not the run's document inventory. gap_reconciliation cannot close free-text absence gaps against core_filings/documents_read. The chair consumes those findings and gaps verbatim, and there is no post-check of 'no issuer filing' claims against core_filings.state=ready.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL2-3, escalated: F10, F16, two gaps and a chair key point deny holding any issuer release or filing beside the cited 10-Q and Item 2.02 8-K.

defects.title: Latest-quarter regression: Q3 issuer operating data lost; Q2 presented as the latest (carries PYPL2-2)
defects.root_cause: The recency pass is capped at 4 lexically ranked items. With web articles stored in the window (yahoo/tradingview 10-27, startupfortune 10-29) and the anchor at the run day (newest_held 2026-11-02), the 4 slots can be filled by web chunks or ER table fragments without headline figures. The outcome is not deterministic (PYPL2 hit t18; PYPL3 did not). facts_read=0 means no structured ER channel backs the question.
defects.fix: Regression from PYPL2 (carries PYPL-1/PYPL2-2). The ADR-076 recency pass ran but its window was anchored on the run day (newest_held 2026-11-02, the pre-amendment rule). PayPal was not rerun after #316.

defects.title: Litigation and regulatory picture falsely empty (carries PYPL2-4)
defects.root_cause: material_risks ran one generic corpus intent (8 items) with no legal/regulatory intent aimed at Note 13 / Part II Item 1. Absence gaps are written from the question's window, not from the indexed 10-Q.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-2/PYPL-3 (PYPL2-4).

defects.title: Executive synthesis draws an engagement conclusion from a single third-party monthly-actives figure
defects.root_cause: The editor validates citations, figures and prohibited words but not the source class of the cited finding for non-event claims. ADR-078 covers only material corporate events.
defects.fix: ADR-078 covers material corporate events only; nothing checks the source class of a cited finding for other claims.

defects.title: Leverage called 'manageable net debt' on long-term debt alone (carries PYPL2-7)
defects.root_cause: ADR-067 withholds total debt, so the narrative falls back to the long-term-debt line. No payments playbook or customer-funds-aware leverage view exists.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-4 (PYPL2-7).

defects.title: Buybacks larger than FCF are hidden behind 'other uses not quantified' (carries PYPL2-8)
defects.root_cause: The secfin line set lacks PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock, and the ER capital-return bullets are not read.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-8 (PYPL2-8).

defects.title: False 'not in evidence' gaps for figures tagged in the held 10-K/10-Q XBRL
defects.root_cause: get_sec_statements returns a fixed line set and periods (FY2025 + one current-quarter revenue). Investigators write absence gaps from that tool output, and gap reconciliation does not check companyfacts for the named line and period.

defects.title: Company unclassified; mining/industrial template gaps persist (carries PYPL2-6)
defects.root_cause: Unchanged: no SIC 7389 mapping, and description inference refused. The web follow-up template also uses capacity vocabulary.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-6 (PYPL2-6).

defects.title: CEO change missing (carries PYPL2-9)
defects.root_cause: Item 5.02 8-Ks and the DEF 14A are outside the acquired set. The governance question had a single corpus intent.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-9 (PYPL2-9).

defects.title: Competitive position 'Evidenced' with no competitor (carries PYPL2-12)
defects.root_cause: Contract satisfaction counts evidence items and distinct sources, not answering findings. The section label follows from any finding.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-10 (PYPL2-12).

defects.title: Irrelevant and rumour items in current developments (carries PYPL2-11)
defects.root_cause: No relevance or claim-status filter on catalyst_evidence. ADR-078 covers summaries, not this list.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-12 (PYPL2-11).

defects.title: numeric_verification withholds 4 correct statements (carries PYPL2-13)
defects.root_cause: Unchanged.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL-13 (PYPL2-13).

defects.title: Trust ladder types user-agreement terms as 'corporate_event'; red team withheld
defects.root_cause: W4 classify_claim's _EVENT_RE is lexical (it likely matched 'trademark'/'waiver'). The safety-gate drop is all-or-nothing per agent.

defects.title: Period and identity labelling slips persist (carries PYPL2-14)
defects.root_cause: financial_statements_state counts only the issuer-document fact channel. Web findings get no period parse.
defects.fix: Carries PYPL2-14.

defects.title: Another registrant's (an SEC-registered U.S. equities/options exchange) business model, customer concentration and governance are filed as Cellectis's, labelled 'issuer filing', and lead the executive synthesis
defects.root_cause: Web search admitted an SEC-hosted exchange financial-statement exhibit (Form 1 annual amendment style, Cboe EDGA/EDGX) into the Cellectis corpus. The sec.gov domain mapped it to source class regulatory_filing / kind issuer_filing with no registrant (CIK/name) check against the subject. That is the same path that brought the Calyxt-era FY2022 20-F in CLLS2. The investigator wrote 'The company…', so ADR-066/074 subject guards (which key on a named other company or on the other company's own domain) never fired. The gap writer saw the mismatch, but gaps do not veto findings, and the editor (citations/figures/prohibited words) does not check meaning.
defects.fix: #315 2ea310a (ADR-079) relabelled the page third_party_filing but kept it on CLLS4 (CLLS4-1). #317 6df9d89 (ADR-079 review) drops a CIK-less EDGAR page whose text never names the subject. Live on CLLS5 36d046bc: statements_about_other_registrant=2, an entity_ambiguous gap, the CLLS4 F1-F3 invalidated, and 0 exchange statements in findings, sections, synthesis or chair. Residue in rendered gaps only (CLLS5-6).

defects.title: The H1 2026 interim report is now held (ADR-077) but none of its figures reaches a finding; the report's cash figure is Q1 2025

defects.title: ADR-079 relabels the other registrant's SEC page as 'third party filing' but does not drop it: F1–F3 still describe an equities exchange as 'The company' and lead the Business model section and executive-synthesis sentence 1
defects.root_cause: apply_edgar_registrant ran (the kind changed to third_party_filing), but the verdict was not 'other'. Both 'unidentified' and 'counterparty' map to third_party_filing and are kept by design. 'unidentified' is the likely one: either (a) the URL that edgar_registrant reads for a search_company_corpus hit does not carry /Archives/edgar/data/<CIK>/ (ADR-079 notes that reports do not store a web chunk's URL; if the item's URL is missing or is a non-archive form, no CIK is read), or (b) _resolve_edgar_subject failed silently ('any failure leaves nothing known, so every page is unidentified'). A lexical 'counterparty' match is less likely, because the exchange exhibit should not name Cellectis. Second layer: outside competitive_position nothing treats a third_party_filing statement worded 'The company…' as not about the subject. The section renderer and the editor (which checks citations, figures and prohibited words, not meaning) present it as the subject's business. The fix's tests evidently cover the URL-bearing path, not the live corpus-hit item shape.

The page was sec.gov/Archives/edgar/vprr/2600/26000283.pdf, a paper filing with NO CIK, so ADR-079 left it 'unidentified' and kept it. #317 6df9d89: a CIK-less EDGAR page whose text never names the subject is 'other' and dropped (replay over all 15 jobs: this PDF is the only CIK-less EDGAR URL, in CLLS, CLLS2 and CLLS4). shelved.status: draft, shelved after 4 review rounds; left open with an explanatory comment
shelved.summary: Four rounds of independent adversarial review found 13, 19, 21 and 38 false drops of true statements (deny-list, narrower deny-list, full-period allow-list, strict adjacency). Guidance verbs ('lifted FY2026 revenue to', 'set at', 'cut to') and trailing qualifiers ('is the midpoint of its range') read as actuals. Conclusion: actual versus guidance cannot be decided by wording rules after the fact; it needs a statement-kind tag at extraction. ADBE-3 stays OUTSTANDING P1.

hypotheses.evidence: Fixed live: another company's statement cited from its own site (South32, Lundin, Ecora: ANTO 10/35 -> 0/40, ADR-074); another SEC registrant's exhibit found by web search on sec.gov and labelled issuer_filing from the host alone (P0 CLLS3-1: a Cboe EDGA exhibit became 'The company operates a single reportable segment: an electronic market...' and led the Cellectis synthesis). #315 (ADR-079) only relabelled it, because the page was a CIK-less paper filing (P0 CLLS4-1); #317 drops a CIK-less EDGAR page that never names the subject, and CLLS5 shows it gone (statements_about_other_registrant=2, entity separation 2 -> 5). All four final reruns (PYPL3, CLLS3, CLLS4, CLLS5) had a degraded element: CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5 used the deterministic chair fallback, which states '0 finding(s) ... No model was available' although the chair slot is routed to azure_openai and the council actually refused on a blocking question (CLLS2-3); PYPL3's red team was withheld whole by the safety gate (council 7 of 8, PYPL3-13). Completeness also over-states: blocking questions 'satisfied' without their metric (JPM-11) or with 0 findings (PYPL2-12); 'Evidence: Strong' on a report with a P0 (HON before).

hypotheses.name: Discovery triage
hypotheses.evidence: relevance_score_pre_scan was constant per source in every stored run (B 90 x3; D 86/66; E 80.5/60.5; E2 85/30/20) and did not drive the order (E2 shows 30 above 85). Web items got 45 circular theme points or 0. The cap of 15 silently cut 8 E2 names, including 6 of 7 theme-verified web candidates (inferred from counts; names not persisted). ADR-070 scores dynamic items on the intent and half-weights unverified themes; ADR-073 applies relevance before the cap and records funnel.beyond_cap. Residual by design: relevance is the last sort key after eligibility tier and verified-pass counts, so a size-unknown mega cap can still outrank a better-fitting small cap (D5/D7). Live on E3 b14b96d9 (95ba5f7): web scores now vary (65 theme-verified vs 42.5 unverified) and each recomputes on the intent; 3 of 7 admitted web names returned (E2: 1 of 7); the cut is named, by ticker only. Registry scores are still constant (curated 85 x6, platform 75 x4); the score basis of admitted MEI, ILU and KNI says no verified statement names the theme, contradicting their A3 verification; a verified size outranks fit, so 4 admitted names were cut while theme-unverified ABX and ATR were returned (E3-2); theme verification never satisfies the industry constraint, so every web name ranks below all 10 registry names, including adjacent SCCO, CLF and FCX (E3-1). Thesis fit stayed 12/15.
