priorities.title: Period tagging: a forward target date is never the document's period
priorities.problem: The period tagger takes the first half-year expression in an excerpt as the evidence period, so a release that says 'runway into H2 2028' or 'data in H2 2027' is filed as a 2028-H2 or 2027-H2 document. The period-agreement guard then discards statements that combine it with a results filing.
priorities.evidence: CLLS5-1 (P1): the only H1 2026 figure, the net loss that CLLS4 stated exactly, was discarded over periods ['2026-H1', '2028-H2']; the 10-28 6-K is called an 'interim report for period 2027-H2' and 6-K/A-period items are labelled 2027-Q4. CLLS4-2 (P1): the pivot and .HEAL 6-Ks reach findings only as metadata tagged 2027-H2 and 2028-H2. Related period-key defects: ANTO-10 (every 2025/2026 finding None), CLLS-7, PYPL2-14 (Dec-2025 comparatives keyed Q3 2026), PYPL3-14 (web findings with period_key None), C3; related guard damage ANTO-4/ANTO2-2.
priorities.affected: Observed on Cellectis (CLLS4, CLLS5); the tagger and the guard serve every issuer whose releases name future dates (every biotech, every company that guides)
priorities.benefit: Stops the platform from discarding the figures that ADR-076, ADR-077 and #316 now deliver; makes recency, supersession and the period-agreement guard trustworthy.
priorities.scope: Small-medium: take the period from the filing's report date (EDGAR reportDate, the 6-K/A period_end, the results-release heading) and never from a target-date phrase; tag forward dates as targets, not periods; the period-agreement guard ignores target dates and event filings; period keys for web, IR and comparative-column findings (formerly P-11).

priorities.title: One research state derived from the ledger: counts, gaps and 'latest disclosure'
priorities.problem: Gaps, 'latest disclosure', question status, chair counts and the V2 memo contradict the findings in the same report.
priorities.evidence: 16 of 16 claim-audited reports self-contradict. The Cellectis chair says '0 finding(s) ... No model was available' against 37, 37, 38 and 32 ledger findings on four consecutive runs (CLLS2-3); the legacy council says there are no primary filings on every Cellectis run (CLLS-4); PYPL3's chair key point, two gaps, F10 and F16 deny holding any issuer release or filing beside the cited 10-Q and 8-K (PYPL3-1); gaps deny facts that findings state on PayPal, Antofagasta, Cellectis and Lindian (PYPL3-7, ANTO2-3, CLLS2-8, LIN2-4); also PYPL2-3, ANTO-5, LIN-5, ADBE-5, H8, H11; questions 'satisfied' with 0 findings (PYPL2-12, PYPL3-10) or without their metric (JPM-11); 61 vs 73 ADBE gaps.
priorities.benefit: The owner can trust what the page says the platform knows and does not know. Prerequisite for any completeness or readiness label.
priorities.scope: Medium-large: compute newest document, latest period, segment structure and ledger counts once per run; derive gaps and question status from the ledger and inventory; make the chair fallback and the V2 memo read the same state.
priorities.dependency: Benefits from P-3 and P-5; can start independently.

priorities.title: Non-US primary financial extraction: IFRS XBRL, 6-K interim figures, ASX Appendix 5B
priorities.problem: Non-US filings are now acquired (the 20-F, the H1 6-K/A, the Appendix 5B) and none of their statement figures is extracted, so cash, burn, runway and the latest half-year reach the report only by chance through prose.
priorities.evidence: Cellectis: the H1 2026 iXBRL 6-K/A held on CLLS3, CLLS4 and CLLS5 with facts_read=0 on every run (the XBRL reader is us-gaap only); one net-loss line on CLLS4, none on CLLS5; cash is Dec 2025 from a web copy (CLLS5-2) and the 20-F's $208.7m was never read (CLLS2-4). Lindian: the Appendix 5B holds the quarter's cash flow and item 8.7 (4.50 quarters), no runway computed (LIN-2). Antofagasta's documents read 0 facts (ANTO-7). 21 of 26 DOCUMENT_NOT_ACQUIRED gaps and 62 of 114 DOCUMENT_ACQUIRED_EXTRACTION_FAILED gaps are on non-US runs.
priorities.affected: 4 of 4 non-US companies (CFR, ANTO, CLLS, LIN)
priorities.benefit: Current financials, runway and burn for dual-listed and non-US issuers; the biotech and mining playbooks can answer their blocking questions from held filings.
priorities.scope: Large, in slices: (a) ifrs-full XBRL for 20-F filers and iXBRL 6-K/A interims (ADR-077 already selects them); (b) statement tables from non-iXBRL results 6-Ks; (c) ASX Appendix 5B and annual-report layouts; (d) UK RNS/IR results PDFs; (e) the financial questions fall back to the corpus when the fact tools return nothing.
priorities.dependency: P-1 (or extracted interim figures will be discarded by mis-tagged periods). ADR-075 and ADR-077 merged and live.

priorities.title: A claim gate on the synthesis and the chair
priorities.problem: The executive synthesis and the chair state things the ledger does not support: rumours as fact, a wrong business stage, spliced periods, invented counts or disagreements. The P0 class moved: no P0 on the final reruns came from this layer, but nothing yet stops it.
priorities.evidence: P0s PYPL2-1 (takeover rumour as fact), LIN-1 ('mines and sells' for a pre-revenue developer), CLLS-3 ('no FY2024 results'); P1s PYPL2-5 (Q2 figures in a Q3 statement), CLLS2-3, ANTO-5, LIN-6, H11. LIN-1 and CLLS-3 vanished on rerun only because the editor or chair fell back. Final reruns: ADR-078 has never fired in a live run (on PYPL3 the claim was simply not regenerated), and PYPL3-4 shows an engagement conclusion drawn from one third-party figure, outside ADR-078's event vocabulary.
priorities.affected: 5 of 8 companies (HON, PYPL, ANTO, CLLS, LIN)
priorities.benefit: Removes the most damaging P0 class: a confident sentence at the top of the report that is false.
priorities.scope: Medium: claim-type gate for material corporate events (ADR-078, #314, merged); tense/stage check against the ledger's lifecycle facts; period labels carried into chair sentences; chair counts and disagreement ids validated against the ledger; 'not in evidence' never phrased as 'does not exist'.
priorities.dependency: ADR-078 (#314, 48b5777, merged; replay only, not exercised live on PYPL3) covers the material-event part.

priorities.title: Read what was acquired for US filers; never call a held fact 'not acquired'
priorities.problem: US filers' 10-K/10-Q and results EX-99.1 are acquired and indexed, but statement facts beyond the XBRL snapshot are not extracted, and gap writers assert absence from a per-question slice.
priorities.evidence: facts_read=0 for the 10-K/10-Q of HON (before), ADBE, JPM and PYPL; JPM bank KPIs 'not acquired' beside 2,398 indexed chunks (JPM-4); PYPL3 lost the Q3 issuer operating data PYPL2 had (PYPL3-2) and its gaps deny XBRL-tagged FY2024, Q3 2025 and interest-expense figures (PYPL3-7); 114 of 175 audited gaps (all companies) are DOCUMENT_ACQUIRED_EXTRACTION_FAILED.
priorities.affected: 4 US companies (HON, ADBE, JPM, PYPL); the absence-gap check applies to all 8
priorities.benefit: Bank KPIs, TPV and take rate, guidance and buybacks reach US reports; false absence claims leave investor pages.
priorities.scope: Large, in slices: (a) the gap writer checks the corpus, XBRL companyfacts and the document inventory before asserting absence, and uses acquired_not_read beyond recency questions; (b) statement-table extraction for 10-K/10-Q and the Item 2.02 EX-99.1.
priorities.dependency: ADR-068 and ADR-076 (+ amendment) merged. Slice (a) has none.

priorities.title: Subject firewall for implicit subjects, third-party pages and the issuer's own documents
priorities.problem: Statements about counterparties, former subsidiaries and regulated subsidiaries are still filed as the subject's.
priorities.evidence: LIN2-2 (Lindian's own AR risks attributed to Iluka), LIN2-3 (Iluka unit costs answer Lindian's question), CLLS2-2 (Calyxt 2022 risks as Cellectis's counter-thesis), JPM-5 (J.P. Morgan SE ICAAP as group), ANTO2-1 (mine capex as Group), H3 residue (F17, F15). Final reruns: CLLS5-4 (IBA's equipment price as Cellectis industry economics, passed the now-live firewall); the ADR-066 firewall was inert until #315 (FW-1) and has not yet acted in a live run.
priorities.affected: 5 of 8 companies (HON, JPM, ANTO, CLLS, LIN)
priorities.scope: Medium: set scope_key from the evidence entity and table heading, not from prose; a subject check for statements with an implicit subject; former-subsidiary periods from the issuer's own filings.

priorities.title: Acquire the latest non-US results documents
priorities.problem: Non-US issuers are researched on documents one or two periods old because the latest results are never fetched.
priorities.evidence: ANTO FY2025 and H1 2026 results never acquired in either run (ANTO-7; NSM record unreadable, IR PDFs download with a plain GET); Lindian took 5 of 224 ASX documents and missed the Malawi export regime (LIN-7); Cellectis's 6-Ks are now fetched (ADR-077, live on CLLS3-CLLS5). 21 of 26 DOCUMENT_NOT_ACQUIRED gaps are non-US.
priorities.benefit: Current financials for UK, ASX and dual-listed issuers.
priorities.scope: Medium: issuer-IR fallback for results PDFs when NSM fails; rank non-results price-sensitive ASX announcements by risk relevance.
priorities.dependency: ADR-077 (#313, live at selection). Without P-3 the new documents would also go unread.

priorities.problem: Companies without a mapped SEC SIC or stored sector get no playbook, no peers and mining/industrial template questions.
priorities.evidence: PYPL unclassified in all three runs (SIC 7389); ANTO unclassified in both runs; Cellectis unclassified until ADR-075; Lindian sector null; ADBE no software playbook; HON on a stale A&D SIC; mining templates still run on a classified biotech (CLLS2-7).
priorities.benefit: Sector-relevant questions (TPV and take rate, copper reserves and C1, runway and burn, ARR and RPO) and credible peers.
priorities.scope: Medium: SIC 7389 and description-based fallback; non-US classification from the issuer's description; software and payments playbooks; templates keyed by playbook; refresh after corporate actions.
priorities.dependency: P-3 and P-5 for the sector metrics to be filled.
priorities.before_owner_testing: YES for sector-specific testing; NO for identity or financial testing

priorities.evidence: JPM-11 (asset quality and capital satisfied without the metric); CLLS2-4 (blocking cash_runway ran 0 tools); PYPL2-12 (questions satisfied with 0 findings); playbook required_metrics have no consumer. Final reruns: cash_runway round 0 still runs tools=[] on CLLS3-CLLS5 and is answered on CLLS5 only by web follow-up; blocking pipeline_state reads 16 items and writes 0 findings on every Cellectis run.

by_hypothesis.name: Corporate actions / economic perimeter
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; FIXED FOR THE US XBRL SNAPSHOT ONLY
by_hypothesis.judgment: Do not trust perimeter handling outside the US XBRL headline numbers. The one case that was fixed (HON) was fixed because the 10-K tags a restated comparative. Anything narrative, segment-level, mine-level or non-US is unguarded, and the campaign found a new perimeter error (ANTO2-1) on day 2 and a share bridge that omits 16m AstraZeneca shares on the final Cellectis run (CLLS5-3).

by_hypothesis.name: Financial taxonomy
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; FIXED ONLY IN THE DETERMINISTIC LAYER
by_hypothesis.judgment: The structured snapshot now fails closed: it withholds rather than publishes a partial or mis-scoped aggregate. Every LLM-written layer (investigator, council, red team, chair, editor) still mixes periods and scopes, and no verifier stops it. 'Fixed' is true only for the deterministic layer.

by_hypothesis.name: Document acquired but fact not extracted
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; LARGEST SYSTEMIC DEFECT; PARTLY MITIGATED FOR RECENCY QUESTIONS ONLY
by_hypothesis.judgment: This is the product's central failure. 'Missing' in a report usually means 'held and not read', and the reader is told it was not acquired. Until statement extraction works for 10-K/10-Q/EX-99.1, 20-F/6-K (IFRS) and ASX/UK annual and quarterly documents, every report under-states what the platform knows and every completeness label is unreliable.

by_hypothesis.name: Subject / counterparty firewall
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; WORSE THAN REPORTED ON DAY 2; WRONG-REGISTRANT SEC PAGES FIXED LIVE (#317); THE ADR-066 FIREWALL WAS INERT UNTIL #315; IMPLICIT SUBJECTS OPEN
by_hypothesis.judgment: Less trustworthy than the day-2 report said. One guard credited since day 1 (the ADR-066 publisher firewall) did nothing in production until #315 on 2026-11-03, and no test caught it. The worst entity error of the campaign entered on CLLS3 through a door no guard watched (a sec.gov web page trusted for its host) and took two PRs and two live reruns to close. Each guard still covers one sentence shape: the run that removed the exchange admitted IBA's equipment price. A reader cannot assume a finding is about the subject, and a guard cannot be counted as working until a live run shows it acting.

by_hypothesis.name: Multi-listing identity
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED ON THE RESEARCH PATH; SEC LINK AND 6-K ACQUISITION FIXED LIVE; INTERIM FIGURES AND THE SECURITY RECORD OPEN; NOT OBSERVED IN DISCOVERY
by_hypothesis.judgment: The platform now finds a dual-listed foreign filer's SEC filings and its latest interim, proven live. It still cannot read the interim's figures, and it shows the reader one listing. Treat any dual-listed non-US company as under-researched until an interim's statement figures reach the report and the security list is persisted.

by_hypothesis.name: Security-code extraction
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; WKN FAMILY FIXED IN CODE; OTHER TOKEN-AS-NAME CASES OPEN
by_hypothesis.judgment: The named example is fixed in code. The general rule (a code, ticker, heading or index is never a company) is not, and Discovery still loses real names to it. Low severity for research, real for Discovery recall.

by_hypothesis.name: Currentness
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; US LATEST NUMBERS PARTLY FIXED AND REGRESSABLE; RECENCY ANCHOR FIXED LIVE; FORWARD DATES CORRUPT PERIOD TAGS; EVENTS AND NON-US INTERIM FIGURES OPEN
by_hypothesis.judgment: The newest numbers reach US reports through XBRL, and PYPL3 shows that coverage can regress from one run to the next. For non-US issuers the platform now acquires the right interim and anchors recency on a real disclosure, proven live on Cellectis, and then a period tagger that reads 'runway into H2 2028' as the document's period throws the figure away. 'Latest' cannot be trusted for any non-US issuer, for anything that is not an XBRL figure, or for the period label of any finding drawn from a release that names a future date.

by_hypothesis.name: V2 / V3 coherence
by_hypothesis.judgment: The investor page and the technical ledger do not describe the same research state, and nothing reconciles them. Gaps, 'latest disclosure' and question status are written per question from a partial evidence slice, not derived from the ledger and the document inventory.

by_hypothesis.name: Council status
by_hypothesis.verdict: CONFIRMED; HEADER FIXED IN CODE; DEGRADED RUNS ARE COMMON AND SIGNALLED UNRELIABLY
by_hypothesis.judgment: The UI can still imply a normal council run. Degraded states are recorded in report data, but one fallback misstates its own count and reason, and the evaluations did not confirm a page-level marker for editor fallbacks. A degraded run was the norm after day 1 (7 of 8 reruns), not the exception, and the Cellectis fallback has misstated its own count and reason on four consecutive runs.

by_hypothesis.name: Discovery triage
by_hypothesis.judgment: As observed, ranking was meaningless: it measured the source, not the fit. After ADR-070 and ADR-073 it measures fit only inside the web source, and only after eligibility, hard passes and size verification. Live on E3 that is not enough: the best-evidenced small caps (Iluka 12th, Meteoric 11th; Lynas and Lindian cut) still sit below adjacent large caps, and a candidate under an announced takeover (Meteoric) is not flagged. Discovery triage is better than before and still not an order a reader can rely on.

spec_section_19.question: Is company research useful today?
spec_section_19.answer: No, not as research. It is a starting point that an analyst must redo. Final overall-usefulness scores: HON 6 (after fixes), CFR 4, ADBE 4, LIN 4, ANTO 4, JPM 3, PYPL 3, Cellectis 3. Seven of eight companies score 3-4 on usefulness at their latest run, after up to 21 merged corrective PRs. At the latest run the 15-dimension mean is 3.47-4.13 for six of eight (Cellectis 3.47 on CLLS5, JPM 3.47, PYPL 3.67 on PYPL3, ANTO 3.80, ADBE 4.00, LIN 4.13); only HON (5.73) and CFR (5.20, never rerun) are higher. PayPal's third run scored below its second (3.87 -> 3.67); Cellectis needed four reruns to move from 2.33 to 3.47, through a P0 regression on the way. HON reached 6 only on its deterministic snapshot. XBRL headline numbers are reliable; business model, competition, catalysts, counter-thesis and sector KPIs are stale, generic or wrong in most reports.

spec_section_19.question: Can important financial numbers be trusted?
spec_section_19.answer: Filed figures quoted with a citation: mostly yes (every FY2025 XBRL figure for ADBE, JPM and PYPL checked exact; CFR revenue, margins and segments PASS). Derived and headline aggregates: only in the deterministic snapshot, where three P0s (HON YoY sign, CFR x1000, JPM total debt 7.7x too low) are fixed and the layer now withholds rather than guesses. Two of those three are verified by replay, not by a live rerun of the affected company. Anything an LLM layer restates (council, red team, chair, synthesis) can carry the wrong period, scope or entity. Trust the cited filed figure; verify everything else.

spec_section_19.question: Can period/scope/entity handling be trusted?
spec_section_19.answer: No. 89 of 323 independently checked claims (28%) are STALE, WRONG_PERIOD, WRONG_SCOPE or WRONG_ENTITY. On the four rerun companies (PYPL, ANTO, Cellectis, LIN) the share was 29% (23 of 78) on the first runs, 21% (18 of 84) on the day-2 reruns and 25% (21 of 85) at each company's latest run (PYPL3, ANTO2, CLLS5, LIN2): one in four checked claims is still stale or mis-attributed after every fix. New scope, period and entity errors appeared on reruns (ANTO2-1 mine capex as Group; LIN2-3 Iluka unit costs unattributed; the P0 exchange-as-Cellectis on CLLS3 and CLLS4, fixed live on CLLS5; forward target dates used as document periods on CLLS4 and CLLS5; IBA's equipment price as Cellectis industry economics on CLLS5).

spec_section_19.question: Is current-event research good enough?
spec_section_19.answer: No. Catalysts/current scores at the latest run: ADBE 2, JPM 2, PYPL 2, CFR 3, CLLS 3, HON 5, ANTO 5, LIN 5. Missed: Cellectis's strategic pivot (on the first three runs; from CLLS4 the exit is stated but the .HEAL programmes, their data dates and the H2 2028 runway are not), Adobe's CEO succession, CFO exit, Semrush and DOJ settlement, PayPal's CEO change and litigation (still on PYPL3), JPM's Q3 results (selection fixed in code) and Apple Card transaction, CFR's Q1 FY27, Avolta disposal and Baume & Mercier sale, Lindian's Malawi export regime. PYPL2 stated an unconfirmed takeover rumour as fact. #314 (ADR-078) merged after that run; on PYPL3 the rumour is absent only because the claim was not regenerated, so the gate has never fired live.

spec_section_19.question: Is Discovery finding genuinely useful new names?
spec_section_19.answer: Rarely. When the intent is read correctly (E2 after ADR-063) it returned 12 on-thesis names of 15, including useful small caps (Pensana, Rainbow, Lindian, ABX, Astron, ETM). Elsewhere: A found 1 name (Cellectis, already known), B 1 strict fit of 3, C nothing, D 2 strict fits of 10. Recall is the bottleneck: name-only mentions are dropped and the registries are mega-cap heavy. E3 (after the ranking fixes) kept 12 of 15 on thesis and returned 3 of 7 evidenced web names (E2: 1), but still ranked adjacent SCCO, CLF and FCX above Iluka and Meteoric and cut Lynas and Lindian.

spec_section_19.question: Is Discovery ranking them sensibly?
spec_section_19.answer: Not as observed. Scores were constant per source and did not drive the order: Lynas ranked 14th with score 20, SCCO 3rd, and size-unknown mega caps outranked evidenced small caps. ADR-070 and ADR-073 fix the scorer input and apply relevance before the cap, but relevance is still the last sort key and size-unknown still passes as eligible. Live on E3 the fix is partial: web scores vary and the cut is named, but registry scores stay constant (85/75) and a verified size outranks fit, so 4 evidenced names were cut while two theme-unverified ones were returned.

spec_section_19.question: Which sectors work best?
spec_section_19.answer: US filers with clean XBRL, for the financial snapshot only: industrials after the fixes (HON 6) and software and payments numbers (ADBE and PYPL figures exact, even on a 52/53-week year). ASX development-stage mining is the best non-US case on facts read straight from ASX documents (Lindian's JORC reserve and resource, licences, ownership and offtake terms PASS; latest-period 6 after ADR-076). Luxury PDFs give good segment and regional facts (CFR 6 of 10 claims PASS).

spec_section_19.question: Which sectors currently work poorly?
spec_section_19.answer: Dual-listed non-US biotech (Cellectis: usefulness 1 -> 2 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 over five runs; the interim is acquired but its figures do not reach the report, no current cash or runway, the new pipeline missing, a P0 wrong-registrant regression on two runs). UK-listed operating mining (Antofagasta: 2 -> 4; unclassified, financial core two periods stale). Banks (JPM 3: industrial semantics, no bank KPIs extracted, a subsidiary leak). Payments (PayPal 3 on all three runs: unclassified, no payments playbook, a P0 on the second run, a latest-quarter regression on the third). Software as research (no playbook, Tempus AI as a peer, dissolved segments). In Discovery: European biotech and small/mid payments (recall).

spec_section_19.question: What is the single biggest remaining generic weakness?
spec_section_19.answer: The platform acquires the right primary documents and does not read them, then writes a research state that is not derived from what it holds. 114 of 175 audited gaps were DOCUMENT_ACQUIRED_EXTRACTION_FAILED; the issuer-document fact channel read 0 facts for HON (before), ADBE, JPM, PYPL, ANTO, Cellectis and LIN (only CFR, 53 facts, and HON after its fix, 10 facts, read any; Cellectis stayed at 0 on all five runs, including three with the H1 6-K/A held); and every one of the 16 claim-audited reports contradicts itself about what it holds. The final reruns add a sharper form of the same weakness: when a figure from a held filing finally reaches a statement, a mis-assigned period tag can discard it (CLLS5-1).

spec_section_19.question: What are the next THREE engineering priorities?
spec_section_19.answer: 1) P-1: period tagging: a forward target date in a document ('runway into H2 2028', 'data in H2 2027') is never the document's period; the period comes from the filing's report date, and the period-agreement guard does not discard a results figure because an event filing beside it names a future date (CLLS5-1, CLLS4-2). 2) P-2: one research state derived from the ledger: chair and tech counts, 'latest disclosure', question status and gaps computed from the findings and the document inventory, so the chair cannot say 0 findings against 32 (CLLS2-3) and a gap cannot deny what a finding states (PYPL3-1, CLLS2-8, ANTO2-3, LIN2-4). 3) P-3: non-US primary financial extraction: ifrs-full XBRL for 20-F filers, statement figures from 6-K interims (the H1 6-K/A held on three Cellectis runs, facts_read=0), and ASX Appendix 5B cash and runway. The claim gate (ADR-078 has never fired live) and US statement extraction follow as HIGH items.

readiness.recommendation: NOT READY beyond private, owner-supervised use. Do NOT resume broad manual owner testing.
reasons: Overall usefulness at each company's latest run is 3-4/10 for seven of eight companies (HON 6; CFR, ADBE, ANTO and LIN 4; JPM, PYPL and Cellectis 3). The fixes made the structured snapshot safer and removed the worst entity error; they did not make the research useful.

Of 9 P0s, 5 are fixed live (H1, ANTO-1, CLLS-3, CLLS3-1, CLLS4-1). C1 and JPM-1 are fix merged, not proven live (CFR and JPM never rerun). PYPL2-1 is not reproduced live and its fix is proven by replay only: on PYPL3 the claim was simply not regenerated and ADR-078 did not fire. LIN-1 vanished only because the editor failed; its root cause is untouched.

The final reruns showed a fix and a regression in the same run: CLLS5 removed the P0 and lost the only H1 2026 figure to a forward-date period tag (CLLS5-1). PYPL3 lost the Q3 operating data PYPL2 had. Gains do not hold from one run to the next.

A guard credited since day 1, the ADR-066 publisher firewall, did nothing in production until #315 on 2026-11-03 (FW-1) because of a swallowed AttributeError, and it has not yet been seen acting in a live run. 'Merged and deployed' is not evidence that a guard runs.

The campaign stop condition is not met: 40 P1s are open, partly fixed or absent without a fix, and 5 more have a merged fix not proven live. None is an external blocker; they are open because of time and scope.

Every one of the 16 claim-audited reports contradicts itself about what it holds, and labels overstate quality ('Evidence: Strong' on a report with a P0; 'complete analysis' with blocking questions unanswered; the Cellectis chair saying 0 findings on four runs). A human approver cannot catch these without independent checking, so human approval before publication remains necessary but is not sufficient.
readiness.allowed_now: Targeted owner checks of what was fixed and rerun live: HON perimeter and EPS, the Antofagasta entity firewall, Lindian's Sep-quarter cash, the Cellectis SEC link and 6-K/A selection, the Cellectis wrong-registrant fix (CLLS5), Discovery materials intent. Not PayPal's Q3 operating data: it regressed on PYPL3.
readiness.gate: P-1, P-2 and P-3 merged, deployed and rerun on at least HON, CFR, JPM, PYPL, Cellectis and Lindian; ADR-078 observed firing in a live run; the live ADR-066 firewall observed acting in a live run (LIN); P-10 (statement kind) at least designed.
readiness.safety: Unchanged: evidence-first, citation-bound, no public recommendations, human approval before every publication, admin-gated routes. The platform remains private-use; the UK NSM and ASX source terms still require consent before any public launch.

Status rule (applied to every defect in this version): a defect counts as fixed only when a live rerun shows it gone (FIXED_LIVE). A merged fix with replay or code evidence only is 'fix merged, not proven live'. A defect absent on a rerun without a targeted fix stays open (NOT_REPRODUCED). CLLS4-4 (Regenxbio) is gone on CLLS5 and the orchestrator's campaign summary calls it fixed; with no PR targeting it this report lists it as NOT_REPRODUCED.

Register IDs PYPL3-x, CLLS3-x, CLLS4-x and CLLS5-x follow each evaluation's own numbering. Many carry an earlier ID (stated in the note column; for example PYPL3-2 carries PYPL-1/PYPL2-2). The register therefore counts some lineages once per run in which an evaluation logged them anew: the P0-P3 totals count register entries, not distinct root causes.
FW-1 (the inert ADR-066 publisher firewall) was found in code while fixing CLLS3-1 (PR #315), not by a report evaluation. Its severity (P1) was assigned by the campaign orchestrator.

Cellectis June 2026 cash in the held 6-K/A: the CLLS3 and CLLS5 evaluations and the orchestrator's campaign summary give $169m; the CLLS4 evaluation gives $166.8m (and H1 burn $29.7m, where CLLS3 gives -$42m). No report stated either figure, so no verdict depends on it; the discrepancy is not reconciled here.

The Calyxt risk text (CLLS2-2): the day-2 evaluation places it in Cellectis's FY2022 20-F; the #317 review traced the CLLS2 case to Cellectis's own 2017 20-F (CIK 1627281) and classed it as staleness, not entity. Either way it is the issuer's own old filing. The register keeps CLLS2-2 under hypothesis D, A with that caveat.

The orchestrator's campaign summary says that on CLLS5 no exchange text remains on any reader surface. The CLLS5 evaluation records two exchange-derived gap texts rendered in section 13 (CLLS5-6, P3). This report follows the evaluation: no exchange statement remains in findings, section leads, the synthesis or the chair; gap residue remains.

Discovery E3: which 4 of the 8 beyond-cap names are web-admitted is a deduction from the funnel counts and the ranking key (most likely CRML, ARA, NB, PKX), not stored data; per-name state is not persisted for cut names (E3-8). The E3 evaluation used stored data plus two ASX announcement-page reads (MEI, KNI) to check the takeover and the market cap.

Its 'playbook captures economics' opens with 'Largely yes' but its own explanation says the economics are not captured; this report reads it as 'No'.
Severity: ADBE-3 (a forecast shown as a reported actual) is P1 in the evaluation but meets the spec's P0 wording ('unsupported claim presented as fact'). Each defect keeps its logged severity here.

Status NOT_REPRODUCED marks defects absent on a rerun with no targeted fix (PYPL-5, PYPL2-5, ANTO-4, CLLS-12, CLLS4-4, LIN-1, LIN-6). They are not counted as fixed.
